transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-09-11
- Time: 09:30 PT
- Duration: 47 minutes (recorded)
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (CSM), Evan (SE), Marta (Silverglen Head of Platform), Damien (SRE), Lina (PM), Omar (Security)

Summary:
Quick kickoff for Silverglen's implementation. Align on stakeholders, network and security constraints, success metrics, and next steps for a pilot. Agreed to a 2-week technical smoke test followed by pilot scope.

Topics:
- Roles and communication cadence
- Network topology, VPC peering and allowlist
- Data retention and KMS/HSM expectations
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and cost guardrails
- Pilot plan and success criteria

Action items (covered above)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Moreno, AE at Redwood Inference. Priya and Evan from our team are here. Quick round robin?
[00:00:12] Marta: Hi, Marta here. Head of Platform at Silverglen. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:00:18] Damien: Damien Park, SRE lead. I'll handle the networking side.
[00:00:22] Lina: Lina Gomez, PM for the internal AI platform.
[00:00:25] Omar: Omar Haddad, security. I'll be the compliance contact.
[00:00:30] Priya: Thanks folks. High level purpose: align on kickoff for implementation and make sure we have a clear pilot runway.
[00:00:36] Alex: Today's goals: agree on stakeholders, get a sense of constraints (VPC, on-prem), define pilot success, and list immediate next steps. Evan, do you want to add?
[00:00:45] Evan: Yeah, I want to understand what you're currently running — are you looking at the hosted API or private deployment? And what models / latency targets?
[00:00:54] Marta: Our initial ask is to move the internal docs-summarization flow to Redwood. We care about median p95 latency under 400ms for single-turn generation. We're currently running an internal microservice on commodity GPUs but the cost/ops are heavy.
[00:01:10] Lina: Also need evaluation on the embeddings route for search; throughput matters there.
[00:01:15] Alex: Great. Any compliance constraints? Omar?
[00:01:19] Omar: We're obligated to keep some PII logs for 30 days for audit but they must be encrypted at rest with keys we control. So KMS/HSM integration and tenant-level key control matter. Also need SOC2 type II evidence and audit logs.
[00:01:38] Evan: We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments; for Hosted API we have a bring-your-key option but there are some nuances on key rotation windows. We'll send the KMS doc.
[00:01:49] Damien: Network: we prefer VPC peering, private endpoints. Can you do peering with our AWS account? Or do you require IP allowlist to an egress?
[00:02:01] Priya: Both are possible depending on the plan. For Redwood Private we do VPC peering or Transit Gateway in many regions. For dedicated pools we can set up private endpoints and an allowlist. Evan, maybe the network checklist?
[00:02:13] Evan: Sure, I can walk through the checklist. We'll need VPC CIDR info, NAT/GW config, any proxy or egress inspection, and the firewall team contact. Also SSH into bastion is optional for on-prem installers.
[00:02:29] [00:02:35] Marta: (overlapping) For our SREs, we want minimal open inbound ports; everything should be egress to Redwood endpoints.
[00:02:40] Evan: Yep that's our common pattern.
[00:02:45] Alex: On the product side, let's align on pilot success criteria. Lina, what would you measure?
[00:02:52] Lina: We need three things: response quality parity with current (score from 0-5 on human evals, target +0.2 improvement), latency p95 under 400ms for 90% of requests, and cost per 1k requests under our target — we will share a baseline cost number.
[00:03:09] Priya: We'll help set up automated evals and a small prompt suite. Evan will own the benchmark template.
[00:03:15] Evan: I'll share a spreadsheet and a small harness that runs loads and captures latency and token costs.
[00:03:22] Damien: For load, we plan to run a 48 hr smoke test with traffic similar to production at 20% scale. Do you support continuous KV cache persists across restarts? We want to test prefix caching behavior.
[00:03:36] Evan: Yes, our runtime has KV cache persistence options; sometimes the term gets mangled in transcription but it's the KV cache / prefix cache. We'll document expected warmup patterns.
[00:03:46] Omar: Back to compliance: what about logs? We need audit logs for model-version rollout, who called what, and redaction hooks for PII.
[00:03:56] Priya: We provide detailed request traces and token-level cost breakdowns in the Console; we can configure retention and redaction. For private deployments, retention is customer-controlled.
[00:04:08] Alex: Any blockers for timeline? Marta, do you have target date for pilot start?
[00:04:12] Marta: We'd like pilot to start in two weeks, ideally 2025-09-25, with the 48-hr smoke test right after staging is up.
[00:04:19] Alex: That's reasonable. We'll aim to deliver sandbox by 2025-09-14 and schedule the SRE deep-dive the following week.
[00:04:26] Lina: On roles: I'll manage product acceptance, Damien will sign off infra, Omar will take compliance sign-off.
[00:04:32] Alex: Great. Next let's surface any procurement or billing constraints.
[00:04:36] Marta: We need a paperless PO option and have standard T&C redlines. Pricing expectation: a short pilot at lower committed price, then evaluate for dedicated capacity if the pilot is successful.
[00:04:48] Alex: We'll share a pilot pricing worksheet. 
[00:04:52] Evan: Technical note: depending on model family and quantization, throughput vs latency changes. We'll provide a recommended config — often teams start with a 16-bit quant profile in Dedicated for latency, or an 8-bit/quant variant for cost savings if latency allowance exists.
[00:05:10] Damien: Can you run the initial benchmark against our sample shard? We'll provide a small dataset.
[00:05:15] Evan: Yes, share s3 bucket access or a secure transfer; we'll consume it and run the harness.
[00:05:22] Omar: Regarding identity, does Redwood support SSO/SAML for console and fine-grained RBAC?
[00:05:28] Priya: Yes — SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported, and RBAC can be configured per-team and per-route. We'll include the SSO guide.
[00:05:36] Marta: Good. Also data residency — some of our EU users need EU-only model endpoints. Is that supported?
[00:05:42] Alex: We have region routing and can pin workloads to regions; for Private we can run in your VPC in eu-west-1 or customer on-prem. We'll document options.
[00:05:51] Lina: A few practical asks from product: 1) an API key rotation window, 2) webhook delivery guarantees for webhook-based callbacks, 3) a retry/backpressure strategy for high concurrency.
[00:06:02] Evan: API keys rotate via the Console or API — we'll include rotation docs. Webhook guarantees are best-effort with queued delivery; we can discuss a durable queue or pubsub integration if you need strict at-least-once. For backpressure we have a rate adaptive circuit that will surface throttling at route-level.
[00:06:18] [00:06:25] (brief silence)
[00:06:30] Alex: Sounds like we have a clear list. I want to call out the pilot scope so we're aligned: one generation route for doc-summarization (single-turn), one embeddings route for search, performance benchmarking, and security/compliance checks.
[00:06:44] Marta: Yes. One more: can you show a quick sketch of the network topology you'd expect for a Private deployment vs Dedicated?
[00:06:51] Evan: Sure — private: we install a control plane that talks over mutual TLS to your VPC with an optional peering; dedicated: Redwood-managed GPUs in a dedicated account with private endpoints into your VPC. I'll send diagrams after the call.
[00:07:04] Omar: And logs will be forwarded to our Splunk collector — is that supported?
[00:07:09] Priya: Yes we have log forwarding via secure syslog or S3 buckets depending on the plan.
[00:07:15] Lina: Any known limitations on multi-tenant data segregation for a Dedicated pool? We need tenant isolation if we share with other teams.
[00:07:22] Evan: Dedicated pools give you tenancy isolation at the node level; we can enforce model pinning and tenant quotas. There are some nuances around shared cache tiers but we'll document isolation guarantees.
[00:07:35] Damien: Network question: latency jitter — do you provide regional failover with graceful degradation?
[00:07:40] Alex: Yes, routing policies can failover to a secondary region or a lower-tier model; there's an automated fallback policy. We'll show examples in the runbook.
[00:07:50] Marta: About runbook — please include a troubleshooting checklist: common causes of latency spikes, model warmup guidance, and guidance on tokenization mismatch across model versions.
[00:07:59] Priya: We'll include that. Also a short on-call rotation recommendation during pilot so your SREs aren't on-call without context.
[00:08:06] [00:08:12] Lina: Can we get an expected timeline for SOC2 docs and encryption attestation? Our auditor will need artifacts within 2 weeks.
[00:08:20] Alex: We can provide SOC2 summary and an SOC2 artifact package; for full attestations some paperwork might take longer but we'll prioritize.
[00:08:30] Omar: We'll still need a SOC2 plus encryption details; send the security pack.
[00:08:35] Evan: I'll attach our security FAQ and a short checklist for compliance that maps to your requirements.
[00:08:42] Alex: Ok let's recap the next steps out loud. Alex will send onboarding runbook, pilot pricing worksheet, and sandbox access timeline; Priya will book the SRE deep-dive; Evan will provision sandbox and send benchmark harness; Damien will share network contacts and sample dataset; Omar will list compliance items the auditor needs; Lina will share product acceptance baseline.
[00:09:07] Marta: That covers it for now. Thanks team.
[00:09:10] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll sync on the calendar.
[00:09:15] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "KV cache" typed as "K V cash" in one doc, "redwood private" sometimes logged as "redwood privatee"; names spelled as 'Marta' sometimes 'Mirtha' by auto-transcript. The content above has been lightly cleaned but retains natural speech patterns and some overlapping talk.
